a.html: Retail analytics is the process of analyzing in-store customer behavior such as footfall, dwell time, movement patterns, queue pressure, and conversion signals to improve store performance.

blocks.q: How does retail analytics work with CCTV?

a.html: Cameras capture video, AI models detect customer movement and behavior, the footage is converted into structured metrics, and dashboards display KPIs for operations, merchandising, and marketing teams.

blocks.q: Can existing CCTV be used for retail analytics?

a.html: Yes. Intelense KenVision connects to existing CCTV, IP cameras, NVR, DVR, or RTSP streams so retailers can measure customer behavior without installing separate sensor hardware.

blocks.q: What retail metrics can Intelense track?

a.html: Intelense can track footfall, entry and exit direction, dwell time, zone occupancy, queue length, heatmaps, customer flow, and conversion from visits to engagement.

blocks.q: Does retail analytics require extra sensors?

a.html: No. Intelense is designed to use the store camera network already in place. Extra sensors can be integrated when useful, but they are not required for core video analytics.

blocks.q: How accurate is AI retail analytics?

a.html: Accuracy depends on camera placement, lighting, and crowd density. Intelense validates each deployment and retail case studies have shown 95 percent footfall accuracy in real store environments.

blocks.q: Is raw video stored in the cloud?

a.html: Deployments can be configured for edge processing so raw video remains within the customer environment while dashboards receive structured analytics and event metadata.

blocks.q: How quickly can a retail analytics dashboard go live?

a.html: When camera streams are available, a pilot can typically be configured quickly with store zones, KPI dashboards, and alerts tailored to the retailer's workflow.

Construction sites enforce safety through a combination of regulations, insurance requirements, and human oversight all of which break down at scale.

The site had multiple active zones heavy machinery areas, restricted zones, pedestrian corridors with no live monitoring across all of them simultaneously.
Cameras were present but monitored by humans who couldn't watch every feed at once. PPE compliance checks were periodic, not continuous creating gaps in enforcement.
Regulatory reporting was manual and time-consuming. Audit trails were incomplete, creating legal and insurance exposure for the contractor and site owner.

128+ Cameras Multi-Zone Site 24/7 Operations Regulatory Mandate

Standard CCTV footage recorded but not analysed. Violations visible only in retrospect during incident review.
Manual patrols safety officers covered a fraction of the site at any time. Non-compliant zones were checked hours apart.
Periodic audits compliance was measured monthly or quarterly, not continuously. Problems compounded between checks.

Hard hats, high-vis vests, and safety boots verified across all zones at all times. Non-compliance triggers instant supervisor notification.
Restricted zones monitored 24/7. Unauthorised entry detected and flagged automatically, reducing liability and securing high-risk areas around the clock.
Dynamic site layout changes tracked in real time. AI adapts to new zones, scaffolding additions, and shifting work areas no manual camera reconfiguration required.
Every incident, alert, and compliance check logged automatically. Regulatory reports generated on demand cutting audit preparation from days to minutes.

blocks.html: How Generative AI Is Rewriting the Rules of Business
Riya Menon Head of AI Strategy, Intelense April 2026 3 min read

blocks.alt: Generative AI concept

blocks.html: In November 2022, OpenAI released ChatGPT. Within two months it had 100 million users — the fastest-growing application in history. Three years on, the hype has become strategy: enterprises are deploying generative AI not as an experiment but as infrastructure.

Microsoft embedded Copilot across Office 365, giving 345 million users AI that drafts, summarises, and generates reports. Salesforce launched Einstein Copilot inside CRM workflows. Adobe built Firefly into Photoshop and Premiere Pro — Coca-Cola and IBM now generate campaign variants at scale, cutting creative iteration from weeks to hours.

"Generative AI is the most transformative technology since the internet — not because it replaces workers, but because it removes the ceiling on what a small team can produce." — McKinsey Global Institute

The clearest ROI is in high-volume, lower-stakes tasks: customer support, code drafting, document summarisation. Klarna's OpenAI-powered assistant handles two-thirds of all customer chats — the equivalent of 700 full-time agents — resolving issues in 2 minutes versus 11 minutes previously.
$4.4T Annual economic impact projected by McKinsey
parts: Annual economic impact projected by McKinsey

blocks.html: 2 min Klarna AI resolution vs 11 min human average
parts: Klarna AI resolution vs 11 min human average

blocks.html: The gap between hype and reality is hallucination — generative models produce confident, wrong answers. Enterprises getting the most value treat AI as a force multiplier, not a replacement, and keep humans in the loop for anything consequential.
Generative AI handles the conversation layer. Operational AI — computer vision, IoT analytics, robotics — handles the execution layer. The most capable enterprises are building both.

Honeywell and Bosch have built AI analytics directly into their commercial camera lines — detecting intrusions, counting occupancy, and flagging unusual behaviour automatically. Avigilon (Motorola Solutions) and Genetec power AI video management for airports, stadiums, and city-wide deployments. Singapore's Safe City programme uses AI video analytics across its entire island-wide CCTV network.

Retail: John Lewis and Tesco use AI video analytics for footfall counting, queue management, and loss prevention — detecting shoplifting patterns in real time, not after the fact.
Manufacturing: BMW uses computer vision on production lines to detect defects invisible to the human eye, reducing quality escapes by up to 90%.
Transport: Transport for London uses AI video analytics across the Underground to detect overcrowding and unattended bags, triggering staff alerts before incidents escalate.

blocks.html: The 9-to-5 Is Being Rewritten: How AI Is Changing the Way We Work
Priya Sharma Operations Analyst, Intelense April 2026 3 min read

blocks.alt: Team collaborating in a modern workplace

blocks.html: AI isn't coming for jobs wholesale — but it is coming for tasks. Goldman Sachs estimates that 46% of tasks in finance and 44% in management are candidates for AI automation or augmentation. That doesn't mean half the workforce disappears. It means what those roles do changes, often dramatically.
Where AI Is Already Embedded at Scale

Microsoft Copilot is live across Office 365 for 345 million enterprise users. Early trials showed a 70% drop in time spent searching for meeting notes, and 68% of users said it helped them return to focus faster after interruptions.

GitHub Copilot — used by over 1.8 million developers at Stripe, Duolingo, and Mercedes-Benz — writes code 55% faster according to GitHub's own research. It's not replacing developers; it's eliminating the tedious parts of their day.

blocks.alt: Developer working with code on multiple screens

blocks.html: "AI doesn't eliminate jobs. It eliminates the parts of jobs people find least meaningful — freeing capacity for judgment, creativity, and relationships."
The Physical Workplace Is Changing Too

On factory floors, AI-guided robotics from ABB and FANUC now work alongside human operators — handling repetitive precision tasks while humans manage exceptions. Amazon's fulfilment centres run over 750,000 AI-guided robots, but human headcount has grown in parallel.

In smart buildings, facilities teams no longer do routine rounds. AI generates alerts when equipment is about to fail, occupancy spikes unexpectedly, or energy use deviates — so people respond to real events, not scheduled checks.

blogs/ai-across-every-sector.desc: From John Deere's precision spraying to NHS radiology AI — a sector-by-sector breakdown of who's deploying AI and what results they're seeing.
blogs/ai-across-every-sector.h1: AI in Every Sector: How Different Industries Are Deploying Intelligent Systems

blocks.html: AI in Every Sector: How Different Industries Are Deploying Intelligent Systems
Karan Mehta Industry Research, Intelense April 2026 4 min read

blocks.alt: Data intelligence across industries

blocks.html: AI is no longer a technology sector story. It's a deployment story happening simultaneously in agriculture, healthcare, logistics, construction, and retail. Here's who's doing what — and what results they're actually getting.

John Deere's See & Spray system uses computer vision to distinguish crops from weeds in real time, applying herbicide only where needed — reducing chemical use by 66%. Climate Corporation (Bayer) uses satellite imagery and AI to deliver per-field yield predictions across over 100 million acres of US farmland.

NHS trusts are using AI radiology tools from Qure.ai to triage chest X-rays and CT scans — catching abnormalities faster than any radiologist working alone. Google DeepMind detected eye disease from retinal scans with 94% accuracy, matching the world's top specialists.

blocks.alt: Modern hospital with technology

blocks.html: UPS's ORION AI routing system saves over 100 million miles of driving annually and cuts 10 million gallons of fuel per year. DHL uses predictive AI to forecast shipment volumes 3 weeks out with 90%+ accuracy, staffing dynamically rather than by historical patterns.

Amazon Go stores use computer vision to track what shoppers pick up and charge them automatically — no checkout required. Zara uses AI demand forecasting to reduce unsold inventory by 30%, critical in fast fashion where overproduction destroys margin.
66% Herbicide reduction with John Deere See & Spray

blogs/ai-digital-billboards.title: Digital Billboards Are Getting Smart: AI Is Personalising Outdoor Advertising | Intelense Blog
blogs/ai-digital-billboards.desc: JCDecaux, Clear Channel, and Lamar are deploying AI that reads the crowd and serves the right ad in real time. How computer vision is transforming OOH advertising.
blogs/ai-digital-billboards.h1: Digital Billboards Are Getting Smart: How AI Is Personalising Outdoor Advertising

blocks.html: Digital Billboards Are Getting Smart: How AI Is Personalising Outdoor Advertising
Sana Kapoor Product Marketing, Intelense April 2026 3 min read

blocks.alt: Digital billboards lighting up a city street at night

blocks.html: Out-of-home advertising has always had a measurement problem. You can count impressions, but you can't know who saw your billboard, for how long, or whether it influenced them. AI is changing that — turning static outdoor media into dynamic, data-driven intelligence systems.

JCDecaux, the world's largest outdoor advertising company, has deployed computer vision systems across its digital panels in Paris, London, and Singapore that analyse crowd composition in real time — age distribution, gender split, dwell time — and serve contextually relevant ads automatically. A panel near a gym at 7am shows protein bar ads. The same panel at lunchtime switches to quick-service restaurant promotions.

Clear Channel launched its RADAR platform, which uses anonymised mobile location data and AI to map audience movement patterns across its entire US network — letting brands buy audiences, not just locations. Lamar Advertising uses AI to optimise creative rotation based on real-time traffic and weather data.

blocks.alt: Busy city intersection with digital displays

blocks.html: "The billboard of 2026 isn't static. It reads its audience and responds in real time — the same way a good salesperson would."
What AI Enables That Was Impossible Before

items: Audience-triggered creative: serve different content based on who's actually present
Dwell time measurement: know how long people actually engage with each panel
Weather and context awareness: dynamically adjust messaging for time of day, temperature, events
Verified reach reporting: move from estimated impressions to AI-confirmed view counts

blocks.html: 40% Higher engagement with AI-personalised OOH creative
parts: Higher engagement with AI-personalised OOH creative

blocks.html: 3× Improvement in audience targeting accuracy vs static buys

blocks.html: $40B+ Global OOH market shifting to programmatic AI buying

blocks.html: The global OOH market is moving toward programmatic, audience-first buying — and computer vision is the measurement layer that makes it possible. Brands that understand this shift are getting more from outdoor media than they ever have.

blogs/ai-construction-safety.title: From Reactive to Predictive: The New Era of AI-Powered Construction Safety | Intelense Blog
blogs/ai-construction-safety.desc: Construction is the world's second-deadliest industry. AI doesn't add more rules — it changes enforcement from periodic and human to continuous and automated.
blogs/ai-construction-safety.h1: From Reactive to Predictive: The New Era of AI-Powered Construction Safety

blocks.html: From Reactive to Predictive: The New Era of AI-Powered Construction Safety
Dev Krishnan Safety AI Specialist, Intelense April 2026 3 min read

blocks.alt: Construction workers wearing PPE on a large site

blocks.html: Construction kills more workers than almost any other industry. In the US alone, 1 in 5 worker fatalities occur on construction sites. In the UK, construction accounts for 40% of all workplace deaths despite employing 7% of the workforce. The safety systems that exist — manual inspections, periodic audits, safety officer rounds — are fundamentally reactive. By the time a violation is documented, the risk has already been taken.
AI doesn't add more rules. It changes the enforcement model from periodic and human to continuous and automated.

Turner Construction, one of the largest US contractors, has piloted computer vision systems that monitor PPE compliance across job sites in real time — alerting supervisors instantly when a worker enters a zone without a hard hat or high-vis vest. Skanska uses AI video analytics to detect unsafe proximity between workers and heavy machinery, triggering audio warnings before an incident can occur.

blocks.alt: Construction site with cranes and scaffolding

blocks.html: "A safety officer can watch one zone at a time. AI watches every camera simultaneously, every second, without fatigue."

items: PPE detection: hard hat, high-vis, gloves, safety boots — per person, per zone, continuously
Human-vehicle proximity: detects unsafe distances between workers and plant equipment
Zone trespassing: alerts when unauthorised personnel enter restricted areas
Fire & smoke detection: AI-powered visual detection, faster than conventional sensors
Automated reporting: audit-ready compliance logs generated without manual paperwork

parts: Reduction in safety violations after AI deployment

parts: Alert time from incident detection to notification

blocks.html: The ROI isn't only in lives saved — though that's the primary metric. It's in insurance premiums, regulatory fines avoided, project delays prevented, and the audit trail that demonstrates due diligence.
KenSafety deploys on your existing cameras in 48 hours — PPE compliance, hazard detection, and automated reporting from day one.

blogs/ai-smart-buildings.title: Your Building Is Wasting Energy Right Now. AI Can Fix That. | Intelense Blog
blogs/ai-smart-buildings.desc: Google cut data centre cooling by 40%. JLL saves 35% on energy across its managed portfolio. Buildings account for 40% of global energy — AI is the management layer that fixes the waste.
blogs/ai-smart-buildings.h1: Your Building Is Wasting Energy Right Now. AI Can Fix That.

blocks.html: Your Building Is Wasting Energy Right Now. AI Can Fix That.
Meera Iyer Smart Spaces Lead, Intelense April 2026 3 min read

blocks.alt: Modern office building at night with energy efficiency systems

blocks.html: Buildings account for 40% of global energy consumption. Most of that energy is wasted — on heating empty rooms, running HVAC systems on fixed schedules regardless of occupancy, and maintaining equipment past its optimal service window. The systems managing most commercial buildings were designed for a world that didn't have the compute to do better.
What Google, JLL, and Siemens Are Doing

Google deployed DeepMind AI to manage cooling in its data centres. The result: a 40% reduction in cooling energy — saving hundreds of millions of dollars annually and reducing carbon emissions from some of the world's most power-hungry infrastructure.

JLL, which manages over 4.6 billion square feet of commercial real estate globally, uses AI-powered building management across its portfolio — delivering an average 35% reduction in energy costs and cutting maintenance spend through predictive failure detection. Buildings under AI management see 20-30% fewer unplanned outages.

Siemens's Desigo CC and Johnson Controls's OpenBlue platforms use AI to continuously optimise HVAC, lighting, and access based on real-time occupancy data — adjusting every 15 minutes rather than following a fixed daily schedule.

blocks.alt: Building management control room with dashboards

blocks.html: "A building that responds to who's actually in it — not who was in it last Tuesday — is a fundamentally different infrastructure cost."
What AI Manages That Humans Can't

items: Occupancy-responsive HVAC: heating and cooling only where people actually are
Predictive maintenance: detecting bearing wear, motor degradation, and filter blockages weeks before failure
Energy benchmarking: comparing consumption against similar buildings in real time
Space utilisation: understanding which meeting rooms, floors, and zones are actually used — informing lease and renovation decisions

blocks.html: 40% Cooling energy reduction at Google data centres
parts: Cooling energy reduction at Google data centres

blocks.html: 35% Energy cost reduction across JLL portfolio
parts: Energy cost reduction across JLL portfolio

blocks.html: The payback period for AI-managed building systems is typically 18 to 36 months. After that, savings compound — because the AI continues learning the building's patterns and optimising as usage changes.
KenHome delivers occupancy analytics, energy optimisation, and predictive maintenance for commercial buildings and campuses — deployed in 48 hours.

blocks.html: When you contact us, request a demo, or create an account, we collect information such as your name, email address, company name, phone number, and the content of your communications with us.

Our AI products process visual and sensor data within your infrastructure. For camera-based products, all video processing occurs at the edge raw video footage is never transmitted to or stored on Intelense servers. Only anonymised analytics outputs (counts, aggregated metrics, event classifications) are retained.

We collect information about how you use our platform, including log files, IP addresses, browser type, device identifiers, and session data. This data helps us improve our products and diagnose technical issues.

items: To provide and maintain our AI products and services
To respond to enquiries, support requests, and feedback
To send product updates, security notices, and marketing communications (with your consent)
To improve our AI models and product performance using anonymised, aggregated data
To comply with legal obligations and enforce our Terms of Service

blocks.html: Data Processing and Privacy by Design
Intelense's products are built on a privacy-by-design architecture:

items: Edge processing: All video analysis is performed locally. Raw footage never leaves your network.
Anonymisation: Individuals captured on camera are not identified or tracked across sessions. Analytics are aggregated and non-identifiable by default.
Data minimisation: We only collect the data necessary to provide our services.
Retention limits: Anonymised analytics data is retained for the period specified in your service agreement, then deleted.

blocks.html: We do not sell personal information. We may share information with:

items: Service providers who assist us in delivering our products (cloud hosting, analytics, support tooling) under strict data processing agreements
Professional advisors including lawyers, auditors, and insurers as necessary
Regulators and law enforcement when required by law or to protect our rights
Successors in the event of a merger, acquisition, or sale of business assets

blocks.html: Intelense operates from Canada and India. Where we transfer personal data internationally, we ensure appropriate safeguards are in place, including Standard Contractual Clauses approved by the European Commission for EU/EEA data subjects.

Depending on your jurisdiction, you may have rights to access, correct, delete, or restrict processing of your personal data. You may also have the right to data portability and to withdraw consent for marketing communications.
To exercise any of these rights, contact us at privacy@intelense.ca. We will respond within 30 days.

Our website uses essential cookies to ensure functionality, and optional analytics cookies to understand how visitors use our site. You may opt out of analytics cookies through our cookie preference centre or your browser settings. We do not use advertising or third-party tracking cookies.

We implement industry-standard security measures including encryption in transit, encryption at rest, access controls, and regular penetration testing. However, no method of transmission over the internet is 100% secure, and we cannot guarantee absolute security.

Our services are not directed to individuals under the age of 16. We do not knowingly collect personal information from children. If you believe we have inadvertently collected such information, please contact us immediately.

We may update this Privacy Policy from time to time. We will notify you of significant changes by email or by posting a prominent notice on our website. The "Last updated" date at the top of this page indicates when the policy was last revised.
